title: PROPOSAL — PAS App Manifest capabilities surface (SR-1 / T2a / AG-3)
description: PROPOSAL ONLY — not wired into production. Companion to docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-07-sr-1-app-isolation-trust-model.md. Defines the UNIFIED capability + tool + per-tool risk-metadata surface so T2a's ToolRegistry (identity/invocation fields), AG-3's agent policy (risk fields), and SR-1's trust tiers (requiresCapabilities) all read ONE object shape. When adopted, these definitions merge into core/src/schemas/app-manifest.schema.json under capabilities.* — they intentionally mirror that file's conventions (additionalProperties:false, lowercase-hyphen ids, handler-relative-path). This file is a design artifact; do not $ref it from runtime code.
$comment: Root here models ONLY the additions to the existing manifest.capabilities object. Existing capabilities.{messages,schedules,rules,events} are unchanged and omitted for clarity; the two new members are `capabilities.declared[]` (Tier A vocabulary) and `capabilities.tools[]` (unified tool + risk surface).

declared.description: Tier A capability vocabulary the app requests. Closed enum; each entry is an operator-visible permission the runtime enforces at inject-time (Tier A), import-time (Tier B), and RPC-boundary-time (Tier C). Absence of a capability = the narrowest default (see design §2.1). This is the least-privilege refinement layer over the coarse requirements.services[] enum.

net.description: Network egress policy. Only meaningful when `net:fetch` is in `declared`. Host allowlist is Tier-B/C ENFORCED (Tier A records it as a truthful permission prompt only).

allow.description: Allowed outbound hosts (exact hostnames, no scheme, no path). Empty or absent with `net:fetch` declared = no hosts permitted until Tier B lands (fail-closed).

tools.description: THE UNIFIED SURFACE. One object per tool. T2a's ToolRegistry reads identity/invocation fields; AG-3/AG-2 read the agent metadata fields; SR-1 trust tiers read requiresCapabilities[]. There is no second array — risk metadata is co-located, not joined by name.

capability.description: A named Tier A capability. Closed enum plus one parameterized family (secrets:<id>, per design §2.1). Extending this enum is a deliberate, reviewed core change. NOTE: reply-scoped messaging is the IMPLICIT baseline, NOT a declared token — any app injected the messenger (requirements.services[] contains 'telegram') may reply to the triggering user without declaring anything, so there is deliberately no `messaging:reply` here (design §2.1). Each declared capability MUST be consistent with requirements.services[] — a normative services<->capabilities validator (design §2.1) rejects a manifest declaring a capability whose backing service is absent, or injecting a privileged service with no declared capability.

anyOf.$comment: secrets:<externalApiId> — grants ONE declared external-API secret via SecretsService. The <id> must match a requirements.external_apis[].id. process.env is never exposed (design §6).

toolDef.description: A single tool. One object shape read by all three consumers (design §3.2).

name.description: Namespaced tool id `app:verb` (e.g. `food:add-grocery-item`). App-id prefix must match the manifest app.id; unique within the app.

description.description: Model-facing tool specification. This is the text the LLM sees; it is FENCED as untrusted app-shipped content in the agent context (doctrine injection posture).

parameters.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the tool's arguments. REQUIRED — T2a's ToolRegistry and the confirmation-gate argument rendering both need a schema-shaped argument spec, so a tool may not omit it. A no-argument tool declares the empty object schema `{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false}` explicitly (Codex Major: omitted parameters previously left the ToolRegistry contract without an arg schema).
parameters.$comment: T2a / ToolRegistry — argument schema. Required. Left as an open object here (a nested JSON Schema); the implementer may tighten to a $ref of a schema-of-schemas.

handler.description: Handler file path relative to app root, mirroring schedule.handler / eventSubscribe.handler conventions in the live schema.

requiresCapabilities.description: The subset of capabilities.declared[] this tool exercises. ToolPolicy REFUSES to register a tool whose requiresCapabilities are not all present in capabilities.declared[] (a tool cannot exceed its app's declared surface). SR-1 trust tiers enforce this same set when the tool runs. Empty = a pure in-memory tool needing no capability.
requiresCapabilities.$comment: SR-1 trust tiers — the link between a tool and the capability model.

riskClass.description: AG-3 risk ladder (doctrine item 4). `read` = no state change; `write` = mutates PAS-owned data; `external-effect` = observable side effect outside PAS (send message, HTTP, audio). REQUIRED at authoring so no tool ships unclassified (AG-3: retrofitting risk classes is the expensive path).

agentAllowed.description: May a bounded agent session (AG-2) call this tool at all. SAFE DEFAULT false — a tool is not agent-callable until deliberately opted in. Structured (non-agent) T2a tool calls ignore this field.
agentAllowed.$comment: AG-3 — agent policy filter. Default false = opt-in.

requiresConfirmation.description: Must the confirmation gate render this tool's ARGUMENTS before execution (doctrine item 4). If omitted, defaults by riskClass: write & external-effect => true, read => false. Config (agent.require_confirmation) may TIGHTEN but never loosen a manifest `true` (per-tool override only via manifest).
requiresConfirmation.$comment: AG-3 — confirmation gate. Explicit value overrides the riskClass-derived default.

costHint.description: Advisory cost signal surfaced in the agent's escalation 'estimated budget' offer. Never an enforcement input (budget enforcement is CostTracker-owned).

allOf.$comment: Confirmation default derivation is documented, not schema-enforced: a validator/loader applies `requiresConfirmation ??= (riskClass !== 'read')`. Encoding the derivation as an if/then would make the field required, defeating the 'defaulted-at-read' design (§3.2). Left to the loader.

examples.$comment: Illustrative — a grocery app's capabilities block under the proposed surface. Reply-scoped messaging is implicit (the app declares 'telegram' in requirements.services[]); only the widenings beyond baseline appear in declared[]. `messaging:any-user` here is the explicit grant that food:notify-household needs.

tools.name: food:list-grocery-items
tools.description: List the current grocery items for the requesting user or their shared space.

tools.name: food:add-grocery-item
tools.description: Add an item to the grocery list.

tools.name: food:notify-household
tools.description: Message every household member that the grocery run is happening.
